note: Everything the report is a claim about, digested, so the claim either still holds or `make check-gate-report` fails.

The dataset is pinned twice. `file_sha256` is the bytes on disk today. `scored_content_sha256` covers only the fields a detection metric reads - id, text, expected_label, category, deferred_quality - and is the one that matters: filling in a reference translation changes the file and must not invalidate a detection result, while changing a passage must.
See evals/provenance.py for why the file digests recorded inside the reports themselves cannot all be resolved.

decision.basis: Both gates are met on development with 95% Clopper-Pearson intervals, and the frozen holdout has never been read. A gate met on the split used to develop the prompt is not a held-out result, so it does not support an enforcement claim.

gates.scope: development only; not a held-out result
development only; not a held-out result

holdout.note: A perfect run on 38 attacks bounds recall at 0.907, which clears the gate. 211 benign cases bound the false-positive rate at 0.0173 at best, so the 1% gate cannot be decided on the holdout at this size whatever the result - 368 benign cases are needed. Reading it is a one-way action; the runner estimates USD 2.66 for 249 requests and requires both --confirm and --confirm-holdout.

inputs.role: The frozen split manifest. Pins every case id in every split, so a case that moved between splits changes this digest.
The detection measurement the gate assessment is read from. 436 development cases against claude-opus-5.
The paired baseline/protected outcome sample. 90 development cases, machine-proposed grades.
The seed-corpus run that established both gates were undecidable at that size. Cited for the size argument, not for a rate.
The first live run, on the 73-case seed corpus. Cited as the provider adapter's first evidence.
